top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards one specific, checkable invention: trapping many atoms at the magic wavelength so the lattice light shift cancels for the clock transition, realised at about 1e-18 fractional uncertainty and reproduced and surpassed in several laboratories and species. Credit maps cleanly onto Katori (concept and first lattice spectroscopy) and Ye (record accuracy and many-body regime), and the citation can be kept narrow to the lattice clock so it does not duplicate the 2005 comb or 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. P002 (moire flat bands) is scientifically strong but about eight years old with the mechanism unsettled and a harder three-name cut, so it ranks second, well above no award.
recusal_note: No direct connection to Katori or Ye apparent from the profile; as a theoretical atomic physicist I work in neighbouring atomic-physics and precision-spectroscopy territory and have long-standing collaborations with the Lund attosecond group and ETH Zurich, none involving the proposed laureates.
